If I could change the world in one way, I would erase the concept of *otherness*—the idea that difference (in nationality, race, belief, species, or even time) justifies hierarchy, violence, or indifference. Not by forcing uniformity, but by making the reflex of empathy so instinctive that exploitation, war, and ecological ruin would feel as unthinkable as harming one’s own hand.
